_about: The ONE contract of the direct road's WEB ↔ SHELL bridge (story 4993 · 4c-1). The web (a page the SERVER serves) asks the shell — which owns the socket — to open a direct road to one paired computer, to send ONE command over it and to read how a command came out. The shell decides what may ride the road (the web is not trusted with that), and everything that goes back to the web is a CLOSED WORD or a number: never an address, a port, a ticket, a key, nor a free text. Both the shell's lib/directBridge.js and the web's wiring (PR 5) read this file; a change of any word here is a new bridge version.

reply.command_id: the press key of this ask (only when ok)
reply.envelope: the sealed ask — the page POSTs it to the server (only when ok)
reply.phone_key_id: this phone's key id for that POST (only when ok)
reply.why: open_why word (only when ok is false)

direct.ask.note: (version 2 · 4c-2) The PAGE carries the negotiation through the server; the shell only seals and opens. This makes the sealed ASK for a door (box-proved, with a one-time key of this try) and holds the try for its minute: the page POSTs the envelope to /desktop/computers/{id}/direct and reads the Mac's sealed answer back. ok:false is not an error: the web goes on by the server. A computer that failed a moment ago answers why 'cooling' at once (five quiet minutes); a try already held or a road already open answers 'busy'.

args.envelope: the Mac's sealed answer exactly as the server gave it

reply.why: open_why word (only when ok is false)

direct.offer.note: The Mac's sealed answer, as the page read it from the server, opened HERE against THAT ask — the pinned computer's signature, the hash of the ask, a private address, then the key agreement; only then the shell dials, says its AEAD hello and verifies the Mac's proof (ok:true = the road is open). The shell judges the answer as bytes: a changed byte, an answer of another ask or another computer, a refusal, a stale one → nothing is dialled and the Mac rests five minutes. The try is SPENT by this call: the same answer again (or any answer for a press key the shell does not hold) answers why 'no_ask' and dials nothing.

reply.why: send_why word (only when sent is false)

direct.send.note: Send ONE command row over the open road. `sent:true` only after the Mac's SIGNED receipt of exactly that command was verified; anything else is sent:false and the web posts the same row (same command_id) to the server — the Mac never runs one command id twice. The shell judges what may ride (see `allowed`) BEFORE a byte is written.

reply.code: the word the Mac's flow ended in (shape [a-z0-9_]{1,64}; after a done, a failed or a rejected one; absent for pending · unknown · a plain done)
reply.got: (only for a file download that is `pending`, once its first piece is in; absent otherwise — a reader that does not know it ignores it) how many pieces of the file the shell has taken: a whole number, 1..of
reply.of: (with `got`) how many pieces the whole file is: ceil(size / 48 KiB), 1..171. Numbers only — never a byte, a name or a hash

direct.result.note: How a command sent over the direct road came out (the Mac says it in a `result` frame; the shell keeps the last 64 for five minutes). `unknown` = the shell has none for that id (never sent that way, forgotten, or the road ended): the web asks the server as before.

direct.close.note: End the road to that computer (the person left the screen). Never a failure. Commands still waiting for a word read as `unknown` afterwards (the web asks the server, as it does for any command it did not send this way).

direct.status.note: Where the road to that computer is now; the web uses it to decide whether to try a send.

reply.code: a closed code of the files road: unknown_request · busy · incomplete · cancelled · save_failed (only when ok is false)

direct.download_save.note: (version 3 · file direct) A download the web sent over the road (a `file_download` row by `direct.send`) is whole and checked when `direct.result` says `done` (with its `size`): this hands the file to the OS share sheet under the name the shell kept when the person picked it, exactly as the server road's `files.download_step` does — the page never sees a byte. `direct.result` for a download answers `pending` · `done` (only for a whole file whose sha-256 is the one the Mac named) · `failed`/`rejected` with the Mac's closed word (`too_big`, `not_enabled`, `road_full`, `bad_file`, `incomplete`, `timeout` …) · `unknown` (the road ended: ask the server for the file from the start — there is no resume). One download at a time (`direct.send` says `busy` for a second).

command_row.session_key: null, or a string of 1..200 characters
command_row.created_at: an ISO 8601 text (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[.fraction](Z|±hh:mm)) of a real moment in the years 2000..2999, 20..40 characters

allowed._note: Decided by the SHELL, from the row's own bytes. The direct road is a plain TCP line on a LAN (until the AEAD wiring lands it shows the whole command; after it, only a length): an instruction's words ride it only sealed, and every kind that has a signature rides it only with one. The Mac judges the same again (a plain send_prompt is refused there too).

file_download.envelope: an object (the phone's own sealed, device-key-signed request — the Mac opens it by the same pin · signature · replay mark as on the relay)

signed_kinds.payload_has: signed: a non-empty string of at most 16384 characters

result_frame._note: What the Mac writes into a `result` frame (inside the connection's cipher): ONE JSON object, exactly these keys, shape-closed words only. The shell drops anything else.
result_frame.spelling: {"command_id":"<id>","state":"done|failed|rejected"[,"code":"<word>"]} — exactly this text: keys in this order, no space; `code` is `[a-z0-9_]{1,64}` (the shape the server itself accepts for a command's result — the whole union of the words the Mac's flows end in): it follows a done too (a stop's commands_running · an instruction's after_step · a clock press's words) and a failed or a rejected one always has it

rows_allowed.name: a download request (sealed · signed by the phone, no session)

result_frames._note: What the Mac writes (state, code → text) and what the shell takes (text → state, code): the same texts both ways. `code` is dropped when it is not the shape; a failed or rejected one without a good word is written with `error`.

good.name: an answer already given (the other phone's)

written_as.name: a failed one with no word is written with `error`
a rejected one with a word that is not the shape is written with `error`
a done with a word that is not the shape is written plain

rows_not_allowed.name: a plain instruction (the words in text)
an instruction with text AND an envelope
a kind that stays on the server (a files read)
a door ask is not sent over a road
a row with a key that is not a command's
a download with a session key
a download with a key that is not its own
a download of a project id that is no id
a download whose envelope is not an object
